newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes almost flat, quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes almost flat, quiet trade.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate reversed early gains and fended off liquidity pressures to close down five basis points at 28.25 percent on Friday, traders said.
"Although dealing was slack, speculation manipulated rates somewhat. Some withheld money, taking advantage of heavy demand for liquidity," a trader said.
"Nonetheless, rates did not vary much precisely because dealing was light," he added.
Bank overnight rates meanwhile closed up 20 basis points at 29.50 percent.
Credit maturities totaled just one billion pesos during the session, but an estimated eight billion pesos in tax bills and pre-weekend demand for cash squeezed liquidity considerably.
Banco de Mexico offset liquidity shortfalls by injecting 7.487 billion pesos by auctioning four credits, which it assigned at rates of between 29.94 and 30.18 percent.
Traders said the approaching holiday season and lack of news had slowed down trading.
"The market is currently awaiting first-half inflation figures for December, which would give us an idea of how high price rises will be for the month as a whole," a dealer said.
Banco de Mexico was expected to announce inflation figures for the first half of December on Monday.
